page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing a constrained-core configuration. Hosted on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance provisions 4 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include support for AVX, AES-NI, VAES, SHA-NI, and BMI2 instruction sets, while lacking AVX-512 extensions. The server pairs these 4 vCPUs with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Local persistent ephemeral capacity is provided via a bundled 322 GB solid-state drive, eliminating reliance on network storage for temporary files and swap spaces. No dedicated GPU hardware is installed. Compute benchmark data demonstrates a distinct divergence between single-threaded and parallel processing. Single-core performance tests such as stress-ng register in the upper quartile (2702.28), while multi-core compute metrics like Geekbench multi-core (3646.0) and PassMark CPU (6181.49) score in the lower quartile due to the 4-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks also record modest throughput, with large-block uncached reads reaching 39.33 GB/sec and writes at 22.83 GB/sec.

This constrained-core design provides qualitative cost advantages for software environments licensed per core, such as enterprise relational database engines. By delivering 64 GB of memory across only 4 active cores, it minimizes core-based software licensing expenses while retaining sufficient memory capacity. Primary operational tradeoffs include limited parallel processing capability and moderate I/O throughput, with Redis SET benchmarks recording 4.11 million operations per second and static web throughput achieving 5.19 GB/sec. Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is primarily suited for memory-intensive relational databases, in-memory caching tiers, intermediate ETL stages, and memory-constrained enterprise applications.
description: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine featuring a constrained-core architecture designed to reduce per-core licensing expenses. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz on Microsoft Hyper-V, it delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of memory and a bundled 322 GB local SSD. Single-threaded execution exhibits solid efficiency, evidenced by strong stress-ng single-core results, though overall multi-threaded throughput remains bounded by the 4-vCPU allocation. The server includes hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, and AVX instructions, but omits AVX-512 extensions and contains no discrete GPU accelerators. With an expansive 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, this instance trades maximum multi-core parallelism for high memory density and localized scratch storage, making it well fitted for enterprise databases, Redis caches, and memory-heavy backend workloads requiring constrained core counts.
